business_problem: The challenge: Connecting large amounts of data from different sources
solution_summary: The challenge: Connecting large amounts of data from different sources Stadtwerke München (SWM), the municipal utilities company serving Munich, has made it its mission to drive every aspect of the city's energy, heating, and mobility transition forward. Making this happen hinges on establishing smart connectivity for all areas of infrastructure. What are required are maximum-efficiency processes, such as predictive infrastructure maintenance and optimized operations planning. For example, during peak times there are up to 500 buses on the streets of Munich. Each of the fleet's electric buses must be relied upon to manage at least 280 kilometers on a single charge-whatever the weather. And Munich has plenty of data to offer: each subway train alone sends values for over 2,000 data points to SWM-and does so every 10 seconds. Geothermic solutions collect around five gigabytes of data every hour. These are just two of about 30 digitized areas of infrastructure.

solution_components.name: Azure Databricks
solution_components.role: Processes and transforms large datasets for analytics, modeling, and downstream reporting.

solution_components.name: Azure IoT
solution_components.role: Collects telemetry from field devices and operational assets into the analytics platform.

data_flow: Operational telemetry is collected through Azure IoT processed in Azure Databricks.
business_outcome: Ensuring the city has an entirely carbon-neutral supply of district heating when needed, having plants capable of producing as much green electricity as the city consumes
